rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass: a bent, slightly elevated bar with a subordinate ground piece, and it is consistent across all four views. The silhouette is not a stair-step collage; it has a continuous upper sweep with a clear hierarchy. The top view shows the main body responding to the parcel orientation rather than merely filling a rectangle, and the road frontage edge is acknowledged by a visible ground response/void at the access side. Programmatically, this is plausible for neighborhood living: it can support active ground threshold plus a compact upper program, with enough openness to read as a public court or entry seam. It is not perfect—the void is modest and the ground articulation remains somewhat small relative to the mass—but it does not collapse into an arbitrary sculptural object. The references collectively support this language: courtyard/bridge/terrace logic, compact neighborhood massing, and a calm upper body over an active lower condition. No hard gate failure is visible, and the mass appears structurally and semantically repairable without major reauthoring.
